principles.strictIsolation: A non-zero approximation score can never be presented as strict phonetic construction.
principles.visibility: The source word/image keeps its real complete pronunciation; the target sound and every edit remain inspectable in data/UI intended for professionals.
principles.clinical: No approximation tier is automatically eligible for clinical use. A professional mode must opt in explicitly if such material is ever exposed.
principles.percentage: The displayed percentage is an editorial weighted edit heuristic, not a scientific phonological-distance or clinical score.
principles.shortSegments: Short chunks are deliberately harder to approximate because one changed phoneme represents a large fraction of the sound.
principles.vowelCloseness: Vowel substitutions are not treated as interchangeable: a small aperture contrast such as /e/↔/ɛ/ costs less than a distant oral or nasal-vowel change. These classes are editorial safeguards, not a phonetic-distance model.
